source_text: Ἔτι δὲ καὶ πρὸς τὸ πεῖσαι ὑμᾶς ὅτι τῶν γραφῶν οὐδὲν συνήκατε, καὶ ἄλλου ψαλμοῦ τῷ Δαυῒδ ὑπὸ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος εἰρημένου ἀναμνήσομαι, ὃν εἴς Σολομῶνα, τὸν γενόμενον καὶ αὐτὸν βασιλέα ὑμῶν, εἰρῆσθαι λέγετε· εἰς δὲ τὸν Χριστὸν ἡμῶν καὶ αὐτὸς εἴρηται. Ὑμεῖς δὲ ἀπὸ τῶν ὁμωνύμων λέξεων ἑαυτοὺς ἐξαπατᾶτε. Ὅπου γὰρ ὁ νόμος τοῦ κυρίου ἄμωμος εἴρηται . οὐχὶ τὸν μετ᾿ ἐκεῖνον μέλλοντα ἀλλὰ τὸν διὰ Μωσέως ἐξηγεῖσθε, τοῦ θεοῦ βοῶντος καινὸν νόμον [ΙS., II, 3; LI, 4; MICH., IV, 2] καὶ καινὴν διαθήκην [JÉR., XXXI. 34, et IS., LIV, 3; Hébr., VIII, 7-8] διαθήσεσθαι. Καὶ ὅπου λέλεκται· Ὁ θεός, τὸ κρίμα σου τῷ βασιλεῖ δός , ἐπειδὴ βασιλεὺς Σολομὼν γέγονεν, εἰς αὐτὸν τὸν ψαλμὸν εἰρῆσθαί φατε, τῶν λόγων τοῦ ψαλμοῦ διαρρήδην κηρυσσόντων εἰς τὸν αἰώνιον βασιλέα, τουτέστιν εἰς τὸν Χριστόν, εἰρῆσθαι. Ὁ γὰρ Χριστὸς βασιλεὺς καὶ ἱερεὺς καὶ θεὸς καὶ κύριος καὶ ἄγγελος καὶ ἄνθρωπος καὶ ἀρχιστράτηγος καὶ λίθος καὶ παιδίον γεννώμενον καὶ παθητὸς γενόμενος πρῶτον, εἶτα εἰς οὐρανὸν ἀνερχόμενος καὶ πάλιν παραγινόμενος μετὰ δόξης καὶ αἰώνιον τὴν βασιλείαν ἔχων κεκήρυκται, ὡς ἀπὸ πασῶν τῶν γραφῶν ἀποδείκνυμι. Ἵνα δὲ καὶ ὅ εἶπον νοήσητε, τοὺς τοῦ ψαλμοῦ λόγους λέγω. Εἰσὶ δ᾿ οὗτοι· Ὁ θεὸς, τὸ κρίμα σου τῷ βασιλεῖ δὸς καὶ τὴν δικαιοσύνην σου τῷ υἱῷ τοῦ βασιλέως, κρίνειν τὸν λαόν σου ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ καὶ τοὺς πτωχούς σου ὲν κρίσει. Ἀναλαβέτω τὰ ὄρη εἰρήνην τῷ λαῷ καὶ οἱ βουνοὶ δικαιοσύνην. Κρινεῖ τοὺς πτωχοὺς τοῦ λαοῦ. καὶ σώσει τοὺς υἱοὺς τῶν πενήτων, καὶ ταπεινώσει συκοφάντην· καὶ συμπαραμενεῖ τῷ ἡλίῳ καὶ πρὸ τῆς σελήνης εἰς γενεὰς γενεῶν. Καταβήσεται ὡς ὑετὸς ἐπὶ πόκον καὶ ὡσεὶ σταγὼν ἡ στάζουσα ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν. Ἀνατελεῖ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις αὐτοῦ δικαιοσύνη, καὶ πλῆθος εἰρήνης ἕως οὗ ἀνταναιρεθῇ ἡ σελήνη. Καὶ κατακυριεύσει ἀπὸ θαλάσσης ἕως θαλάσσης καὶ ἀπὸ ποταμῶν ἕως περάτων τῆς οἰκουμένης. Ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ προπεσοῦνται Αἰθίοπες, καὶ οἱ ἐχθροὶ αὐτοῦ χοῦν λείξουσι. Βασιλεῖς Θαρσεῖς καὶ νῆσοι δῶρα προσάξουσι., βασιλεῖς Ἀρράβων καὶ Σαββᾶ δῶρα προσάξουσι. καὶ προσκυνήσουσιν αὐτῷ πάντες οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς, καὶ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη δουλεύσουσιν αὐτῷ· ὅτι ἐρρύσατο πτωχὸν ἐκ δυνάστου, καὶ πένητα ᾧ οὐχ ὑπῆρχε βοηθός. Φείσεται πτωχοῦ καὶ πένητος, καὶ ψυχὰς πενήτων σώσει· ἐκ τόκου καὶ ἐξ ἀδικίας λυτρώσεται τὰς ψυχὰς αὐτῶν, καὶ ἔντιμον τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν. Καὶ ζήσεται καὶ δοθήσεται αὐτῷ ἐκ τοῦ χρυσίου τῆς Ἀρραβίας, καὶ προσεύξονται διὰ παντὸς περὶ αὐτοῦ· ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν εὐλογήσουσιν αὐτόν. Καὶ ἔσται στήριγμα ἐν τῇ γῇ. ἐπ᾿ ἄκρων τῶν ὀρέων ὑπεραρθήσεται· ὑπὲρ τὸν Λίβανον ὁ καρπὸς αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐξανθήσουσιν ἐκ πόλεως ὡσεὶ χόρτος τῆς γῆς. Ἔσται τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ εὐλογημένον εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας· πρὸ τοῦ ἡλίου διαμένει τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ. Καὶ ἐνευλογηθήσονται ἐν αὐτῷ πᾶσαι αἱ φυλαὶ τῆς γῆς· πάντα τὰ ἔθνη μακαριοῦσιν αὐτόν. Εὐλογητὸς κύριος, ὁ θεὸς Ἰσραήλ, ὁ ποιῶν θαυμάσια μόνος. καὶ εὐλογημένον τὸ ὄνομα τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα καὶ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα τοῦ αἰῶνος· καὶ πληρωθήσεται τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ πᾶσα ἡ γῆ. Γένοιτο, γένοιτο. Καὶ ἐπὶ τέλει τοῦ ψαλμοῦ τούτου, οὗ ἔφην, γέγραπται· Ἐξέλιπον οἱ ὕμνοι Δαυΐδ, υἱοῦ Ἰεσσαί . Καὶ ὅτι μὲν βασιλεὺς ἐγένετο ἐπιφανὴς καὶ μέγας ὁ Σολομὼν, ἐφ᾿ οὗ ὁ οἶκος ὁ ἐν Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἐπικληθεὶς ἀνῳκοδομήθη, ἐπίσταμαι. ὅτι δὲ οὐδὲν τῶν ἐν τῷ ψαλμῷ εἰρημένων συνέβη αὐτῷ, φαίνεται. Οὔτε γὰρ πάντες οἱ βασιλεῖς προσεκύνησαν αὐτῷ, οὔτε μέχρι τῶν περάτων τῆς οἰκουμένης ἐβασίλευσεν, οὔτε οἱ ἐχθροὶ αὐτοῦ ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ πεσόντες χοῦν ἔλειξαν. Ἀλλὰ καὶ τολμῶ λέγειν ἃ γέγραπται ἐν ταῖς Βασιλείαις ὑπ᾿ αὐτοῦ πραχθέντα, ὅτι διὰ γυναῖκα ἐν Σιδῶνι εἰδωλολάτρει · ὅπερ οὐχ ὑπομένουσι πρᾶξαι οἱ ἀπὸ τῶν ἐθνῶν διὰ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ σταυρωθέντος ἐπιγνόντες τὸν ποιητὴν τῶν ὅλων θεόν, ἀλλὰ πᾶσαν αἰκίαν καὶ τιμωρίαν μέχρις ἐσχάτου θανάτου ὑπομένουσι περὶ τοῦ μήτε εἰδωλολατρῆσαι μήτε εἰδωλόθυτα φαγεῖν.
pass_a_gloss: And yet also towards persuading you that you have not understood the scriptures, and I will remind you of another psalm spoken by David through the Holy Spirit, which you say was spoken about Solomon, who also became your king, but it was also spoken about our Christ. You deceive yourselves from the homonymous words. Where the law of the Lord is said to be blameless, you do not explain the one who is to come after him, but the one through Moses, God proclaiming a new law and a new covenant. And where it has been said: God, give your judgment to the king, since Solomon became king, you say the psalm was spoken about him, the words of the psalm clearly proclaiming about the eternal king, that is, about Christ. For Christ is king and priest and God and Lord and angel and man and general and rock and child born and sufferer become first, then ascending into heaven and coming again with glory and having an eternal kingdom, as I show from all the scriptures. So that you may also understand what I said, I will speak the words of the psalm. They are: God, give your judgment to the king and your righteousness to the son of the king, to judge your people in righteousness and your poor in judgment. The mountains will receive peace for the people and the hills righteousness. He will judge the poor of the people and save the sons of the poor, and he will humble the deceitful. He will endure with the sun and before the moon for generations of generations. He will come down like rain upon the fleece and like drops dripping upon the earth. Righteousness will arise in his days and an abundance of peace until the moon is taken away. And he will rule from sea to sea and from rivers to the ends of the earth. The Ethiopians will fall down before him, and his enemies will lick the dust. The kings of Tarshish and the islands will bring gifts, the kings of the Arabs and Saba will bring gifts. And all the kings of the earth will worship him, and all the nations will serve him, because he rescued the poor from the powerful and the poor who had no helper. He will have mercy on the poor and the needy, and he will save the souls of the poor, he will redeem their souls from usury and from injustice, and his name will be honorable before them. And he will live and be given gold from Arabia, and they will pray for him always, they will bless him all day. And he will be a support in the earth, he will be exalted above the tops of the mountains, his fruit will be above Lebanon, and they will blossom from the city like grass of the earth. His name will be blessed forever, his name endures before the sun. And all the tribes of the earth will be blessed in him, all the nations will bless him. Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel, who alone does wonders. And blessed is the name of his glory forever and ever, and the whole earth will be filled with his glory. Let it be, let it be. And at the end of this psalm, which I mentioned, it is written: The hymns of David, the son of Jesse, have ended. And I know that Solomon became a great and famous king, on whom the house in Jerusalem was built. But it is clear that none of the things said in the psalm happened to him. For not all the kings worshiped him, nor did he reign to the ends of the earth, nor did his enemies fall down before him and lick the dust. But I also dare to say what is written in the Kingdoms, that he did idolatry through a woman in Sidon, which those from the nations, knowing the creator God through Jesus the crucified, do not tolerate, but they endure all insult and punishment until the last death, concerning not idolizing or eating idol sacrifices.
pass_b_english: I will remind you of another psalm spoken by David through the Holy Spirit to persuade you that you have not understood the scriptures (John 1:14). You claim this psalm was spoken about Solomon, who also became your king, but it was also spoken about our Christ (John 1:14). You deceive yourselves with these homonymous words. When the law of the Lord is said to be blameless, you do not explain the one who is to come after him, but the one through Moses, God proclaiming a new law and a new covenant (Isaiah 2:3, Isaiah 51:4, Micah 4:2, Jeremiah 31:34, Isaiah 54:3, Hebrews 8:7-8).

And where it is said, 'God, give your judgment to the king, since Solomon became king,' you say the psalm was spoken about him. Yet the words of the psalm clearly proclaim about the eternal king, that is, about Christ. For Christ is king and priest and God and Lord and angel and man and general and rock and child born and sufferer become first, then ascending into heaven and coming again with glory and having an eternal kingdom, as I show from all the scriptures (John 1:14).

So that you may also understand what I said, I will speak the words of the psalm. They are: 'God, give your judgment to the king and your righteousness to the son of the king, to judge your people in righteousness and your poor in judgment (Micah 4:2). The mountains will receive peace for the people and the hills righteousness. He will judge the poor of the people and save the sons of the poor, and he will humble the deceitful. He will endure with the sun and before the moon for generations of generations (Psalm 72:5).'

He will come down like rain upon the fleece and like drops dripping upon the earth. Righteousness will arise in his days and an abundance of peace until the moon is taken away. And he will rule from sea to sea and from rivers to the ends of the earth. The Ethiopians will fall down before him, and his enemies will lick the dust. The kings of Tarshish and the islands will bring gifts, the kings of the Arabs and Saba will bring gifts. And all the kings of the earth will worship him, and all the nations will serve him, because he rescued the poor from the powerful and the poor who had no helper (Psalm 72:10-12).'

He will have mercy on the poor and the needy, and he will save the souls of the poor, he will redeem their souls from usury and from injustice, and his name will be honorable before them. And he will live and be given gold from Arabia, and they will pray for him always, they will bless him all day. And he will be a support in the earth, he will be exalted above the tops of the mountains, his fruit will be above Lebanon, and they will blossom from the city like grass of the earth (Psalm 72:16-17).'

His name will be blessed forever, his name endures before the sun. And all the tribes of the earth will be blessed in him, all the nations will bless him. Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel, who alone does wonders. And blessed is the name of his glory forever and ever, and the whole earth will be filled with his glory. Let it be, let it be (Psalm 72:18-19).'

And at the end of this psalm, which I mentioned, it is written: 'The hymns of David, the son of Jesse, have ended.' And I know that Solomon became a great and famous king, on whom the house in Jerusalem was built. But it is clear that none of the things said in the psalm happened to him. For not all the kings worshiped him, nor did he reign to the ends of the earth, nor did his enemies fall down before him and lick the dust (Psalm 72:11).'

But I also dare to say what is written in the Kingdoms, that he did idolatry through a woman in Sidon. This is what those from the nations, knowing the creator God through Jesus the crucified, do not tolerate. Instead, they endure all insult and punishment until the last death, concerning not idolizing or eating idol sacrifices (1 Corinthians 8:4-6).
